Rashi on Niddah 58b:10:1.english: [If] she did not sit, [she may] not - And we do not say: Perhaps she sat and was not paying attention.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:13:1.hebrew: לדברי אין קץ - שאיני נותן שיעור, ואם לא הרגה, אפילו כחרדל טמאה:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:13:1.english: According to my words, there is no limit - For I do not set a measure, and if she did not kill [a louse], even [if it is as small as] a mustard seed, she is impure.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:13:2.hebrew: ולדברי חברי אין סוף - שהם מקילים יותר מדאי, דאפילו לא הרגה תולה, ואין נותנין שיעור, אלא אפילו כסלע תולה או יותר:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:13:2.english: And according to the statement of my colleagues, there is no end - For they are excessively lenient, as even if she did not kill [a louse], she attributes [the stain to it], and they do not establish a limit [on its size], but rather even [a stain as large as] a sela she attributes [to it], or more.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:16:1.hebrew: עד כגריס - ואפילו לא הרגה, ויתר מכגריס לא, ואפילו הרגה. ולדבריו יש לטמא כגריס ועוד, ולטהר פחות מכגריס:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:16:1.english: Up to the size of a split bean - And even if she did not kill [a louse]; and more than a split bean [she may] not [attribute it], even if she did kill [one]. And according to his statement, there is [reason] to declare impure [a stain of] a split bean and more, and to declare pure [one of] less than a split bean.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:16:2.hebrew: עד כמה - כלומר, וכי אפשר לתלות כתם גדול במאכולת:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:16:2.english: Up to how much - That is to say, is it possible to attribute a large stain to a louse?

Rashi on Niddah 58b:16:3.hebrew: אמר ר"נ תולה בפשפש עד כתורמוס - כתם רחב כתורמוס יכולה לתלות, ולא במאכולת אלא בפשפש, שמא פשפש הרגה, שכתמו גדול. פשפש - פונייש"א בלע"ז:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:16:3.english: Rav Naḥman said: She may attribute [it] to a bedbug up to [the size of] a lupine - A stain as wide as a lupine [seed] she may attribute—and not to a louse, but rather to a bedbug, for perhaps she killed a bedbug, whose stain is large. Pishpesh is punaise [bedbug] in Old French.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:17:1.hebrew: ברית כרותה לו - כלומר, ריחו נודף ומבאיש, וכל המוללו על כרחו מריח ריחו:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:17:1.english: A covenant is made with it - That is to say, its odor wafts and is foul, and whoever rubs it perforce smells its odor.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:17:2.hebrew: לענין כתמים - דאי הוה כתם ארכו כרחבו, אפילו יותר מכגריס תלינן בפשפש:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:17:2.english: With regard to stains - For if a stain's length is equal to its width, even [if it is] larger than a split bean, we attribute [it] to a bedbug.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:18:1.hebrew: או שטעם טעם פשפש - באוכל תרומה מיירי, וכ"ש חולין, דהא שרץ הוא. אלא האי דנקט תרומה — משום דפליגי לעיל מיניה: אמרו לו נטמאת ונטמאת התרומה, ר"א אומר: יבלע, ר' יהושע אומר: יפלוט. אבל אומר לו: טמא היית וטמאה היתה התרומה, או שנודע שהוא טבל, או שטעם טעם פשפש לתוך פיו — ה"ז יפלוט; הואיל ועד שלא נתנה לתוך פיו אירע בה פסול זה, לא חיישינן להפסד תרומה:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:18:1.english: Or if he tasted the taste of a bedbug - [The mishna] is dealing with one eating teruma. And all the more so [in the case of] non-sacred food, for [a bedbug] is a creeping creature. Rather, the reason [the mishna] mentioned teruma is that they disagree earlier in that [mishna]: [If] they said to him, "You have become ritually impure and the teruma has become ritually impure," Rabbi Eliezer says: He should swallow [it], and Rabbi Joshua says: He should spit [it] out. But [if] one says to him, "You were ritually impure and the teruma was ritually impure," or if it became known that it was untithed produce, or if he tasted the taste of a bedbug in his mouth — this [person] must spit [it] out; since this disqualification occurred to it before he put it into his mouth, we are not concerned about the loss of teruma.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:18:2.english: How does he know - The taste of a bedbug?

Rashi on Niddah 58b:18:3.english: And still, how does he know - For surely he did not smell it.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:19:1.english: Pigs - They eat creeping and crawling creatures and splatter blood.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:19:2.hebrew: דדוקרת - טבחים הרבה, ואשפות ושקצים מצויין בה:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:19:2.english: [The town] of Dukeret - [There are] many butchers, and garbage heaps and creeping creatures are common in it.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:1:1.hebrew: שתיהן טמאות - ולא תלינן אחד מן הכתמים בצפור, ואע"ג דאיכא למתלי. וה"נ, אע"ג דבדקה, לימא שתיהן טמאות, דאימור לאו יפה בדקה:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:1:1.english: Both of them are impure - And we do not attribute one of the stains to the bird, even though there is [basis] to attribute [it]. And here too, even though she examined [her robe], let us say [that] both of them are impure, for say that she did not examine [it] thoroughly.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:1:2.hebrew: סלע יתירה - ומאי חזית דתלית ליה לסלע יתירה דטמאה בהך? תלייה בהך! הלכך שתיהן טמאות. אבל הכא, טומאה תלויה בהך דלא בדקה:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:1:2.english: An additional sela - And what did you see to attribute the additional sela that is impure to this [woman]? Attribute it to that [one]! Therefore, both of them are impure. But here, the impurity is attributed to the one who did not examine [her garment].

Rashi on Niddah 58b:22:1.hebrew: והכא לחומרא - הילכך עד ולא עד בכלל, דאי עד ועד בכלל הוה ליה קולא, דקתני עד כגריס תולה. וקיימא לן באלו טריפות (חולין נה.) דבכל עד אזלינן לחומרא: אי עד ועד חומרא הוא אזלינן בתריה, ואי עד ולא עד חומרא הוא אזלינן בתריה:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:22:1.english: And here [it is] for a stringency - Therefore, [here the meaning is] "up to, but not including," for if [it meant] "up to and including," it would be a leniency, as it teaches: "Up to a split bean she may attribute [the stain]." And we maintain in [the chapter] Elu Tereifot (Chullin 55a) that with every [instance of] "up to," we follow the stringency: if [interpreting it as] "up to and including" is a stringency, we follow it; and if [interpreting it as] "up to, but not including" is a stringency, we follow it.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:24:1.english: Some say it on its own - And not in reference to the mishna.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:24:2.hebrew: ה"ג וקמיפלגי בעד ועד דהכא - כדאמר רב הונא לחומרא, כדאמרינן בכל דוכתי, הלכך עד ולא עד בכלל, ולרב חסדא כרבי אבהו:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:24:2.english: This is the reading: "And they disagree regarding 'up to' and 'up to' here" - As Rav Huna said: [It is interpreted] for a stringency, as we say in all places; therefore, [here the meaning is] "up to, but not including"; and according to Rav Ḥisda, [it is] in accordance with Rabbi Abbahu.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:2:1.english: Three robes - One on top of the other.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:2:2.hebrew: יכולה לתלות - כדמפרש, עברה בשוק של טבחים:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:2:2.english: She is able to attribute - As [the baraita] explains: "She passed through a butchers' market."

Rashi on Niddah 58b:5:1.english: How much may she attribute - To the blood of a louse.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:5:2.hebrew: כגריס - אבל טפי מהכי אין דם מאכולת כל כך גדול, ובהכי מיהא תלייה:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:5:2.english: The size of a split bean - But more than this, the blood of a louse is not so large, and to this [extent] at least she attributes [it].

Rashi on Niddah 58b:5:3.hebrew: ואע"פ שלא הרגה - ורבי חנינא פליג אדרבנן, דקאמרי: הרגה - אין, לא הרגה - לא:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:5:3.english: And even if she did not kill [it] - And Rabbi Ḥanina disagrees with the Rabbis, who say: [If] she killed [a louse], yes; [if] she did not kill [one], no.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:5:4.english: And she may attribute [it] to her son and to her husband - If they have a wound.

Rashi on Niddah 58b:5:5.hebrew: ואם יש בה מכה - יבשה וראויה להגלע, כלומר להתלחלח ולהוציא דם, תולה:
Rashi on Niddah 58b:5:5.english: And if she has a wound - [Which is] dry, but capable of reopening — that is to say, to become moist and discharge blood — she may attribute [the stain to it].

Rashi on Niddah 58b:9:1.english: Eye salve - A red plaster [Old French: emplastre].

Tosafot on Niddah 58b:14:1.hebrew: אין לך כל מטה ומטה - הכא לא נקט סדין וסדין כדבסמוך, משום דהכא בעי למימר מטה, אפילו של איש, שאין בה כמה טיפין של דם מאכולת; אם כן, ה"נ של אשה יש לנו לתלות במאכולת. אבל בסמוך לא איירי אלא בשל אשה, להכי נקט סדין:
Tosafot on Niddah 58b:14:1.english: You have no bed of any sort - Here, he did not state "every sheet" as in the adjacent clause, because here he wished to say: [There is no] bed, even of a man, that does not have several drops of louse blood; if so, in [the bed of] a woman as well, we ought to attribute [the blood] to a louse. However, in the adjacent clause, he was dealing only with [the sheet] of a woman; therefore, he mentioned "a sheet".

Tosafot on Niddah 58b:16:1.hebrew: וכדבריו אנו מודים - ומיהו היכא דהרגה הרבה מאכולת או פשפש, תולה כפי מה שהרגה, מידי דהוה אשוק של טבחים:
Tosafot on Niddah 58b:16:1.english: And to his statement we concede - However, where she killed many lice or a bedbug, she may attribute [blood] in accordance with what she killed, just as is the case with a marketplace of butchers.

Tosafot on Niddah 58b:19:1.hebrew: עיר שיש בה חזירים אין חוששין בכתמים - אומר רשב"ם, דאפי' יותר מכגריס, ואפי' מן החגור ולמטה, ואפילו לא נתעסקה, ואין לה מכה שיש לה להגלע ולהוציא דם. מיהו, אור"י דאין לסמוך על זה עכשיו להקל, כשמוצאה כתמים במקום שאין רגילות ליגע בהן חזירים; וכן מנהג, דלא תלינן. ומיהו, במקום שיש רגלים לדבר שיש לתלות בחזירים וכיוצא בהן, תלינן, כדקאמר הש"ס:
Tosafot on Niddah 58b:19:1.english: A town in which there are pigs, one is not concerned for stains - Rashbam says that [this applies] even [if the stain is] larger than a gris, and even [if it is found] from the belt downward, and even if she did not handle [blood] and does not have a wound that is liable to reopen and emit blood. However, the Ri says that one should not rely on this nowadays to be lenient when she finds stains in a place where pigs are not accustomed to touch [them]; and such is the custom, that we do not attribute [stains to pigs]. Nevertheless, in a place where there is a basis for the matter (raglayim la-davar) to attribute [it] to pigs and the like, we attribute [it], as the Talmud says.

Tosafot on Niddah 58b:1:1.hebrew: מאי שנא מהא דתניא ב' נשים כו' - תימה, מה דומה להך דלעיל? דהכא אין לתלות בזו יותר מבזו, אבל לעיל אין לתלות בראשונה, הואיל ובדקה. ואומר ר"ת, דברייתא איירי שנתעסקה בצפור זו אחר זו; ואם היתה נשאלת הראשונה, היינו מטהרין אותה, הואיל ונתעסקה; ובשביל חברתה אנו מטמאין הראשונה, שהיא טהורה גמורה. גם למעלה, אע"פ שהראשונה בדוקה, נטמאנה, הואיל ושניה תולה בה לענין דינא:
Tosafot on Niddah 58b:1:1.english: In what way is [this] different from that which is taught [in a baraita]: Two women, etc. - It is puzzling: How is [this case] similar to that [case] above? For here [in the case of the bird], there is no [reason] to attribute [the blood] to this one more than to that one; whereas above [in the case of the lent garment], there is no [reason] to attribute [the stain] to the first [woman], since she examined [her garment]! And Rabbeinu Tam says that the baraita is dealing with [a case where] they handled the bird one after the other. And if the first [woman] had come to inquire [first], we would have declared her pure, since she handled [the bird]; yet on account of her companion, we declare the first [woman]—who is completely pure—impure. [So too] above, even though the first [woman] was examined, let us declare her impure, since the second [woman] attributes [the stain] to her regarding legal judgment.
